background_notes.fact: For smooth periodic h, S_t h, Dinv h, Dinv2 h, P h and P0 h are smooth; products of smooth periodic functions are smooth. These linear operators preserve reality; S_t preserves the zero Fourier coefficient, while P,Dinv,Dinv2 have zero output coefficient at zero. The map (t,x) -> S_t h(x) is smooth for fixed smooth h.

grounds.reason: Fourier transform convention on the periodic domain.
Smooth means spatially C-infinity and reality is conjugate Fourier symmetry.
Airy multiplier is exp(it k^3) for real t.
P0 extracts the zero Fourier coefficient.
Inverse derivative multiplier is (ik)^(-1) off zero and zero at zero.
Dinv2 is the composition of Dinv with itself.
The induction begins with arbitrary smooth real mean-zero g0 and applies these operations at each step.

background_notes.justification: Integration by parts gives faster-than-any-power decay of smooth periodic Fourier coefficients. The stated multipliers preserve that decay. Any mixed time/spatial derivative of S_t inserts only a polynomial factor in k, so the resulting series converges uniformly on compact time intervals. Inverse derivatives and projections have the claimed zero coefficients. At -k each multiplier is the complex conjugate of its value at k, establishing reality preservation. Product smoothness follows from the Leibniz rule. These facts apply to every finite expression in D009-D011 since tau>0.

background_notes.fact: For fixed smooth periodic f and a finite step [a,b], B_t(f,f) is smooth in (t,x). The stages F(t)=1/2 integral_a^t B_s(f,f)ds, C(t)=integral_a^t B_s(f,F(s))ds and Q(t)=1/2 integral_a^t B_s(F(s),F(s))ds are smooth step functions, with derivatives equal to their respective integrands, and all vanish at a. B_t is symmetric bilinear. If f is real and mean-zero then F,C,Q are real and mean-zero.

grounds.reason: B is S_{-t} partial_x of a product of Airy transforms.
Definition of F as a smooth-step integral.
Definition of C in terms of fixed f and the earlier stage F.
Definition of Q in terms of the earlier stage F.
f=v^n is smooth real mean-zero by the preceding induction; H001 and L>0 give a finite positive step.

background_notes.justification: The Fourier regularity fact BG001 and the product rule give joint smoothness for B, then successively for the integrands defining F,C,Q. On a compact time-space domain, continuous mixed derivatives can be integrated under the integral sign; the fundamental theorem of calculus gives the time derivatives and zero initial values. Spatial differentiation supplies a zero mean before S_{-t}; products, differentiation and Airy transforms preserve reality, as does integration. Symmetry and bilinearity follow directly from the product and the linear operators. In particular 1/2 B_t(f+F,f+F)=1/2 B_t(f,f)+B_t(f,F)+1/2 B_t(F,F), the differentiation identity used in S001.

background_notes.fact: A finite family of continuous functions from closed adjacent time intervals to C-infinity(torus), agreeing at common endpoints, defines a continuous function on their union. If each piece is smooth in time then the resulting function is piecewise time-smooth, with the corresponding one-sided endpoint derivatives.

grounds.reason: Positive integer L gives finitely many grid intervals covering [0,T].
V is defined by the displayed smooth expression on each closed step.
The endpoint calculation establishes V(t_n)=v^n and V(t_{n+1})=v^{n+1}, so adjacent values agree.

background_notes.justification: Within each interval continuity is given. At a shared endpoint both one-sided limits equal the common value; there are finitely many intervals, so this proves continuity everywhere in each C-infinity seminorm (and hence also in the usual weaker function-space topologies). Smoothness on each step gives the stated piecewise regularity. No equality between the derivatives of adjacent pieces is asserted.
